claim_1.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assay analysis of plasma from 212 TIV-vaccinated subjects across the 2007–2011 influenza seasons showed that antibody responses decreased with age in the 2010 and 2011 seasons compared to younger subjects.

sources.section: Results
sources.quote: In the 2010 and 2011 seasons, in which elderly subjects were included, antibody responses showed a significant decrease with age (Figures 1B, 1C, and S1C), consistent with previous studies (Seidman et al., 2012).

claim_2.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assay analysis of plasma from 212 TIV-vaccinated subjects across the 2007–2011 influenza seasons showed no significant difference in antibody response by gender, diabetic status, or race compared to the corresponding contrast groups.

sources.section: Results
sources.quote: There was no significant difference in antibody response based on gender (Figure S1D), diabetic status (Figure S1E), or race (data not shown).

claim_3.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees across multiple influenza seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that interferon-induction and activated dendritic cell blood transcription modules at days 1 and 3 after vaccination were positively associated with day 28 HAI antibody responses compared to modules not associated with high antibody responses.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: BTMs related to the induction of interferons as well as the activation of dendritic cells (Figures 2A and 2B) were enriched on days 1 and 3 after TIV vaccination, whereas modules related to T cells at these time points were negatively associated with the antibody response.

claim_4.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees across multiple influenza seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that T-cell-related blood transcription modules at days 1 and 3 after vaccination were negatively associated with day 28 HAI antibody responses compared to modules associated with high antibody responses.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: BTMs related to the induction of interferons as well as the activation of dendritic cells (Figures 2A and 2B) were enriched on days 1 and 3 after TIV vaccination, whereas modules related to T cells at these time points were negatively associated with the antibody response.

claim_5.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees across multiple influenza seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that antibody-secreting cell and cell-cycle-related blood transcription modules were robustly enriched on day 7 after vaccination compared to earlier post-vaccination time points.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: On day 7, there was a robust enrichment of ASC and cell cycle-related modules, consistent with our original study (Nakaya et al., 2011).

claim_6.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from subjects stratified by gender or race after TIV vaccination showed very few differentially expressed genes compared to the corresponding contrast groups.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: There were very few differentially expressed genes based on gender (Figure S2A) or race (data not shown), indicating similar responses after vaccination.

claim_7.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from type-2-diabetes-positive and type-2-diabetes-negative subjects after TIV vaccination, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed a high degree of overlap in the modules associated with a high day 28 HAI antibody response compared to between-group differences in differential gene expression.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: Comparison of gene expression between type-2-diabetes-positive and -negative subjects revealed a modest number of differentially expressed genes (Figure S2B), but GSEA on genes ranked by correlation with the day 28 HAI response in these two groups showed a high degree of overlap in the modules associated with a high antibody response (Figure S2C).

claim_8.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from subjects across multiple influenza vaccine seasons, using DAMIP, showed that discriminatory gene sets predicted day 28 HAI response in the blind testing group compared to chance classification.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: Here DAMIP was able to correctly predict the HAI response in the blind testing group with 67.6%–70.0% accuracy (Tables S1 and S2).

claim_9.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from subjects across multiple influenza vaccine seasons, using DAMIP, showed that the most frequently selected predictive genes included many antibody-secreting cell genes compared to other gene categories.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: Consistent with our previous work, the most frequently selected genes included a large number of ASC genes (Table S1).

claim_10.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly TIV vaccinees across multiple seasons, using single-sample GSEA and an artificial neural network classifier, showed that blood transcription modules predicted day 28 HAI responses in both young and elderly subjects compared to non-predictive module sets.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: With this approach, we identified BTMs that predicted HAI responses in both the young and elderly groups with accuracies ranging between 79.0% and 80.2% and between 64.7% and 72.3%, respectively, using both day 3 and day 7 signatures (Figure 2C).

claim_11.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly TIV vaccinees across multiple seasons, using single-sample GSEA and an artificial neural network classifier, showed similar classification accuracy in young and elderly test sets when predictive signatures were trained on the young dataset compared to each other.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: Interestingly, we observed similar classification accuracy in both the young and elderly test sets when using the predictive signatures trained on the young dataset (Figure 2C).

claim_12.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects in the 2010 cohort, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that interferon-response and activated dendritic cell modules on day 1 and plasmablast-response modules on day 7 were consistently enriched in both age groups compared to modules not consistently associated with day 28 antibody response.

sources.section: Gene Signatures of Antibody Responses across Multiple Seasons in the Young and the Elderly
sources.quote: There were a number of consistently enriched modules in both the young and elderly, in particular those relating to the interferon response and activation of dendritic cells on day 1 and the plasmablast response on day 7.

claim_13.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from combined influenza vaccine cohorts before vaccination, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that baseline B-cell- and T-cell-related modules were positively correlated with increased day 28 antibody responses compared to baseline modules not associated with increased responses.

sources.section: Baseline Signatures Associated with Antibody Responses
sources.quote: This approach revealed several B-cell- and T-cell-related modules whose expression pre-vaccination was positively correlated with an increased antibody response to vaccination in all studies (Figure 3A).

claim_14.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from combined influenza vaccine cohorts before vaccination, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that baseline monocyte-related modules were negatively correlated with antibody responses compared to baseline modules positively associated with increased responses.

sources.section: Baseline Signatures Associated with Antibody Responses
sources.quote: In contrast, modules related to monocytes were negatively correlated with antibody responses (Figures 3B–3G).

claim_15.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects in the 2010 season after TIV vaccination showed that the largest overall transcriptional difference between age groups occurred on day 1, with young subjects exhibiting many more upregulated and downregulated genes compared to elderly subjects.

sources.section: Signatures Induced by Vaccination with TIV in Young and Elderly
sources.quote: By far the largest difference in overall expression between the two groups occurred on day 1, where the young exhibited a much greater number of both up- and downregulated genes.

claim_16.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects in the 2010 season after TIV vaccination showed that interferon-related genes shared between young and elderly clusters had higher expression magnitude in young individuals compared to elderly individuals.

sources.section: Signatures Induced by Vaccination with TIV in Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Although the genes shared by clusters from young and elderly vaccinated individuals had similar temporal expression profiles, the magnitude of the expression of interferon-related genes differed, being higher in young individuals (Figure 4C).

claim_17.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees in the 2010 and 2011 seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that NK-cell-related modules at days 3 and 7 and monocyte modules at day 7 increased with age compared to younger subjects.

sources.section: Signatures Induced by Vaccination with TIV in Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Natural killer (NK) cell-related modules showed increased expression with age on both day 3 and day 7 after vaccination, and several monocyte modules showed increased expression with age on day 7.

claim_18.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees in the 2010 and 2011 seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that many B-cell modules decreased with age on days 3 and 7 after vaccination compared to younger subjects.

sources.section: Signatures Induced by Vaccination with TIV in Young and Elderly
sources.quote: In contrast, many B cell modules showed decreased expression in older subjects on both day 3 and day 7.

claim_19.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees in the 2010 and 2011 seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that B-cell modules M47.0 and M69 were enriched in younger subjects and in subjects with high antibody responses compared to older subjects and low responders.

sources.section: Signatures Induced by Vaccination with TIV in Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Two B cell modules, M47.0 and M69, showed increased expression in younger subjects and in subjects with high antibody responses, whereas three monocyte- and myeloid-cell-related modules, S4, M4.3, and M11.0, were enriched in the elderly and were also associated with a decreased antibody response in the 2010 and 2011 seasons.

claim_20.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees in the 2010 and 2011 seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that monocyte- and myeloid-cell-related modules S4, M4.3, and M11.0 were enriched in elderly subjects and were associated with decreased antibody responses compared to younger subjects and high responders.

sources.section: Signatures Induced by Vaccination with TIV in Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Two B cell modules, M47.0 and M69, showed increased expression in younger subjects and in subjects with high antibody responses, whereas three monocyte- and myeloid-cell-related modules, S4, M4.3, and M11.0, were enriched in the elderly and were also associated with a decreased antibody response in the 2010 and 2011 seasons.

claim_21.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that total NK-cell proportions were higher in elderly subjects than in young subjects at baseline (day 0) and throughout days 0–14 after vaccination.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Our analysis showed that proportions of total NK cells in elderly subjects were higher than those of young subjects at baseline as well as at all the time points studied (days 0–14).

claim_22.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that vaccination increased the percentage of NK cells in elderly subjects, whereas young subjects showed a reduction in NK-cell percentage on day 1 after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Of note, vaccination induced an increase in the percentage of NK cells in the elderly subjects; in contrast, in the young there was a reduction in the percentage of NK cells on day 1 after vaccination (Figure 5A).

claim_23.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that elderly subjects had a higher frequency of CD56dimCD16++ NK cells and a lower frequency of CD56++ NK cells at baseline compared to young subjects.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: We observed a higher frequency of CD56dimCD16++ cells coincident with a lower frequency of CD56++ cells in the elderly at baseline, consistent with previous studies (Figure 5C; Solana et al., 2014).

claim_24.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that CD56dimCD16++ NK cells increased in elderly subjects on day 1 after vaccination, whereas CD56++ NK cells increased in young subjects on day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: The distribution of these subpopulations was relatively stable during the response, with CD56dimCD16++ cells showing a small but significant increase in the elderly on day 1 after vaccination and CD56++ cells increasing in the young on day 7.

claim_25.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that all three NK-cell subsets in elderly subjects increased CD69 activation after vaccination with highest expression on day 3 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Elderly subjects showed increasing activation after vaccination in all three subsets, with highest expression on day 3.

claim_26.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that young subjects activated the CD56dimCD16++ NK-cell subset by CD69 expression only on day 1 and at a lower level than elderly subjects compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: In contrast, the young exhibited activation of the CD56dimCD16++ subset as measured by CD69 expression only on day 1 and at a lower level than in the elderly.

claim_27.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that monocyte proportions were higher in elderly subjects than in young subjects at baseline and throughout the study compared to young subjects.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: In addition to NK cells, we also observed higher proportions of monocytes among the elderly at baseline and during the entire duration of the study compared to young subjects (Figure S6A).

claim_28.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that total monocyte percentages increased substantially on day 1 after vaccination in both young and elderly subjects compared to baseline (day 0), then returned to or below baseline.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: In both groups, the percentage of total monocytes in PBMCs increased substantially on day 1 after vaccination, then returned to or below baseline levels.

claim_29.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that elderly subjects had a slight increase in intermediate monocytes compared to young subjects.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: The distribution of monocyte subsets was similar in both groups, with the elderly having a slight increase in intermediate monocytes compared to young (Figure S6C).

claim_30.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that CCR5 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes peaked on day 1 after vaccination in both young and elderly subjects compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: In both the young and elderly, CCR5 expression peaked in classical and intermediate monocytes on day 1 after vaccination, corresponding with the inflammation associated with the innate immune response.

claim_31.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that elderly subjects had higher CCR5 expression, whereas young subjects had higher CD86 expression, in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to the opposite age group.

sources.section: Cellular Responses Induced by Vaccination with TIV in the Young and Elderly
sources.quote: Elderly subjects showed increased CCR5 expression in classical and intermediate monocytes compared to the young, whereas young subjects had higher CD86 expression in these subsets.

claim_32.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assay analysis of plasma from a subset of TIV vaccinees measured through day 180 showed that antibody responses peaked at day 28 and declined significantly by day 180 compared to day 28.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: The antibody responses peaked at day 28 (D28), with a significant decline in most subjects by D180 (Figure 6A).

claim_33.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assay analysis of plasma from a subset of TIV vaccinees measured through day 180 showed that day 180 antibody titers depended strongly on the day 28 response compared to subjects with lower day 28 responses.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: Because the D180 antibody titer shows significant dependence on the original antibody response generated on day 28 (Figure 6B), examining the molecular profile associated with the D180 response would identify many of the mechanisms responsible for generating the D28 response.

claim_34.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assay analysis of plasma from a subset of TIV vaccinees measured through day 180 showed that subjects with higher day 28 titers had a greater decrease in HAI response between day 28 and day 180 compared to subjects with lower day 28 titers.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: We observed that subjects with a higher D28 titer had a greater decrease in HAI response between D28 and D180, indicating increased difficulty to maintain higher levels of antibodies.

claim_35.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees showed that day 7 plasmablast module S3 activity was positively associated with day 180 antibody response compared to lower plasmablast module activity.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: As expected, correlation analysis of plasmablast module BTM S3 shows a positive association with the D180 antibody response due to the effect of D28 antibody responses, generated through plasmablast expansion (Figure 6C).

claim_36.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees showed that day 7 plasmablast module S3 activity was not associated with the day 180/day 28 residual compared to the association seen with day 180 antibody response.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: However, when we performed correlation between the plasmablast module activity and the D180/D28 residual, we no longer saw an association with the plasmablast expression (Figure 6D).

claim_37.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that cell movement and adhesion modules including BTM 51 at days 3 and 7 were enriched in subjects with more persistent antibody responses compared to subjects with waning responses.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: Among the BTMs most enriched in subjects with a persistent response on both days 3 and 7 were several modules associated with cell movement and adhesion, such as BTM 51 (Figure 6E).

claim_38.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that day 7 T-cell-related modules were negatively associated with the day 180/day 28 residual compared to subjects with more persistent antibody responses.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: In addition, the day 7 expression of a number of T-cell-related modules was negatively associated with the D180/D28 residual, indicating that increased T cell responses might potentially result in more transient antibody responses (Figure 6F).

claim_39.claim: miRNA expression profiling analysis of samples from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed significant differences in post-vaccination miRNA profiles between young and elderly subjects compared to each other.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: We saw a significant difference in the miRNA profiles between these two groups.

claim_40.claim: miRNA expression profiling analysis of samples from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that most differentially expressed miRNAs in elderly subjects were upregulated after vaccination, particularly on days 1 and 7, whereas young subjects predominantly showed miRNA downregulation compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: Whereas a majority of the differentially expressed miRNA in the elderly were upregulated after vaccination, particularly on days 1 and 7, the young exhibited predominantly downregulation of miRNA.

claim_41.claim: miRNA expression profiling analysis of samples from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort showed that elderly subjects had more miRNAs negatively correlated with day 28 antibody response than young subjects compared to each other.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: We again saw differences between the young and elderly subjects, with the elderly having a larger number of miRNA negatively correlating with the antibody response when compared with the young.

claim_42.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort, integrated with miRNA profiling by correlation analysis, showed groups of blood transcription modules on day 1 after vaccination that appeared to be co-regulated by several miRNAs compared to modules without coordinated miRNA correlations.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: We then performed correlation analysis between all miRNA-BTM pairs, revealing groups of modules that appear to be regulated together by several miRNA (Figure 7D) on day 1 after vaccination.

claim_43.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort, integrated with miRNA profiling, showed that the antiviral interferon signature module M75 on day 1 after vaccination had potential miRNA regulators including miR-424 compared to genes in the module without such predicted negative miRNA correlations.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: Of particular interest was the regulation of module M75-antiviral interferon signature (Figure 7E) on day 1 after vaccination, because the interferon pathway plays a key role during the innate immune response. This miRNA-mRNA network suggests potential novel regulators of the interferon response after vaccination, such as miR-424.
